summary: GPT models straight from OpenAI. Natively supported by PI; an API key is all it needs. Optionally routed through an egress proxy.

requires.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
requires.description: OpenAI API key. PI also accepts a credential stored by `/login openai` instead.
requires.howTo: platform.openai.com -> API keys. Put it in ~/.pi/secrets.env as OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... (chmod 600).

prompts.label: Route OpenAI through an egress proxy or gateway instead of api.openai.com?
prompts.help: Answer yes only for a TRANSPARENT proxy in front of api.openai.com - one that still answers to OpenAI's own model names. Overriding baseUrl on a built-in provider keeps every built-in model and the existing auth, which is exactly right in that case. If the endpoint is a GATEWAY serving its own catalogue (LiteLLM, vLLM, OpenRouter, an in-house router), answer no and choose the `openai-compatible` provider instead: this block would keep OpenAI's model names, and every request would name a model your gateway has never heard of.

prompts.label: Full base URL of the proxy, including the /v1 suffix

validate.message: must be an absolute http(s) URL

notes: NOTHING IS REQUIRED FOR THIS PROVIDER TO WORK. `openai` is built into PI (wire API `openai-responses`). The block above only corrects declared context windows and, optionally, the base URL.

THE OVERRIDES ARE A DELIBERATE DOWNGRADE, NOT A CORRECTION OF A BUG. PI declares 272000 for the gpt-5.6 family and 1050000 for the -pro ids. 272000 is itself PI's own deliberate choice: it is OpenAI's short-context PRICING boundary, and a request one token over it is billed at the long-context rate for the whole request. Capping at 200000 keeps the harness inside that tier with headroom, and keeps the same min(200000, served) rule every other provider here follows. Raise it if you want the room and accept the price change - that is a decision, so make it on purpose.

THE DERIVED baseUrl RESOLVES TO null WHEN NOT PROXYING, AND null MEANS OMIT THE KEY (see config/providers/README.md, substitution rule 3). Writing `"baseUrl": null` or `"baseUrl": ""` into models.json is not the same thing - PI would read it as an override and fail to resolve an endpoint.

A GATEWAY IS A DIFFERENT PROVIDER, NOT THIS ONE WITH A NEW baseUrl. The `useProxy` path above is for a transparent proxy that still serves OpenAI's catalogue. LiteLLM, vLLM, OpenRouter and in-house routers publish their OWN model ids, so pointing this block at one leaves `gpt-5.4` and friends in config/models.json against an endpoint that has never heard of them - an unknown-model error on every request, which reads as a broken install rather than a misconfiguration. Use config/providers/openai-compatible.json, which asks for the model ids and their real context windows.

AZURE OPENAI IS A DIFFERENT PROVIDER, NOT THIS ONE. Use PI's built-in `azure-openai-responses` with AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL, AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION and AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP. It needs no models.json entry at all; add `"openai": "public"`-style egress and concurrency rows for it in routing.json if you route a tier there.

PER-PROVIDER PROXY WITHOUT A GLOBAL ONE. An auth.json credential can carry its own `env` object, applied for that provider only: {"openai": {"type": "api", "key": "$OPENAI_API_KEY", "env": {"HTTPS_PROXY": "http://proxy.example.com:8080"}}}. Prefer that over exporting HTTPS_PROXY globally, which would also capture the local provider.

verify.label: PI sees the provider as configured
